semantics.note: Faithful to the firm present-tense claim. The per-token pricing clause is left out, which is harmless.

contract.note: Reading 'millions of dollars a day' as at least $2M, or even $1M, is an ordinary reading. Limiting it to inference compute in February 2023 matches the context. The result is the same under either threshold.

evidence.note: Reputable reporting (Nov 2023) of the February 2023 SemiAnalysis estimate puts ChatGPT's running cost at about $694k a day. It is an estimate for the same period and metric, and it is below $1M.

reviews.rationale: The only admitted estimate for February 2023 is about $694k a day, below either threshold for 'millions'. No estimate of $1M or more was admitted, and the Forbes source Zitron linked could not be read. On this packet the daily-cost figure is contradicted. 'Extremely expensive' cannot be measured on its own.

contract.note: Tying the claim to AI search or information services presented as authoritative follows the Bing/Bard context. evidence.note: Plaintiff's complaint alleging Gemini contributed to a suicide. These are party allegations, not established causation, and the relationship described was delusional and intimate rather than search-like.
Google's own statement as an interested party, saying it referred the user to crisis help. It neither proves nor disproves causation.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and no dated event in the packet meets the early-resolution rule: the Gavalas causal account is still unadjudicated allegation, and the Guardian piece shows risk only. The claim cannot fail just because nothing has happened yet, so it stays unresolved.

contract.note: The contract scores the causal mechanism even though the speaker hedged it ('from what I can tell'), a tentative-belief qualifier like 'I suspect'. Under the policy, hedged claims are not scored, and a plain reading applies only to firm language.

evidence.note: An independent check shows Bing's pre-recorded demo gave wrong financial figures. This supports the demo-error part only.
Reuters reporting documents the JWST exoplanet error in Bard's launch ad. This supports the demo-error part only.

reviews.rationale: The core causal claim is hedged with 'from what I can tell', so it is not scored. The firm subsidiary fact holds: e1 and e2 show both first demos contained errors. Even if the causal part were scored, nothing in the packet isolates the mechanism, so it would be unresolved.
